thread.title: Apple has delayed the launch of its payment service in India (AAPL)

author: Rachel Green
title: Apple has delayed the launch of its payment service in India (AAPL)
text: Rachel Green 5m This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence " Payments Briefing " subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here . Apple is reportedly delaying its plans to launch a Unified Payments Interface (UPI)-based digital wallet service in India, according to The Economic Times , citing two people familiar with the matter. Apple The UPI is a government-backed interface that enables users to send and receive bank-based payments through smartphones. The decision to delay its service comes after discussions between the tech giant and the National Payments Corporation of India, which manages the UPI. India has provided a substantial opportunity for many companies to go after. The Indian government demonetized in 2016, removing 86% of cash from circulation. That's led to a rapid shift toward digital payments, which created an opportunity that many payments players — particularly big US companies like PayPal, WhatsApp, Google, Amex, and more — moved in on. Many of these players saw quick success: Google Tez, Google's proprietary mobile payments platform design for the Indian market, which just rebranded as Google Pay, added 7.5 million users in the first five weeks of launching, for example. And Paytm, a major India-based mobile payments giant, which added 20 million users in a month following demonetization and 50 million during the next three months, was recently valued at around $10 billion , up from $7 billion in May, demonstrating rapid growth in the space. And there's still ample room for growth, since just 14% of Indian consumers make mobile payments on a weekly basis, which ticks down to 6% on a daily basis. But Apple might not have the same success in the region as other players, so delaying the launch could be a smart move. Despite the region's promise, India is not always an easy market to enter or succeed in. Apple reportedly faced technical and design issues relating to the UPI. But the firm is particularly concerned about the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) new data localization policy, which requires companies to store all of their payments data within India only. This follows recent news of the Indian government reportedly delaying Facebook-owned chat app WhatsApp from launching its payment services in the country — which runs on the UPI and has been in a pilot stage, already reaching 1 million users — due to privacy concerns. Amazon faced obstacles as well while attempting to launch its UPI-based service. On top of that, Apple's reach in India is limited. While the Indian payments space does offer a significant opportunity for firms to develop payment solutions and see high volume, a payment service Apple develops might be limited in scope. That's because the firm holds a small market share in India below 2.5% , compared to Android's dominant 72% market share. That likely cuts into Apple's addressable base, making its potential user base in the market — where mobile payments are just at the beginning of a growth runway — even smaller. Those factors, combined with the crowding in the space as other US-based and international players work to gain market share, likely would have been major hurdles for Apple to overcome — which makes it a good decision for Apple to delay the launch of its service and instead invest resources related to payment services into markets that could be more fruitful as the tech giant pushes to expand Apple Pay.
